## Question And Audience

**Audience:** Public-health analysts preparing an introductory briefing on BMI and income.

**Question:** How does average BMI differ across income groups among adults aged 20–80 in the prepared NHANES classroom dataset?

**Why it matters:** This comparison can help analysts identify a pattern for further investigation while understanding the limits of the evidence.

## Evidence {.smaller}

| Income group | Included records | Average BMI (kg/m²) |
|---|---:|---:|
| High income | 16,330 | 28.6 |
| Middle income | 19,228 | 29.3 |
| Low income | 15,293 | 29.4 |

**Takeaway:** Across 50,851 included records, the rounded
group averages differed by less than one BMI unit.

**Caution:** Descriptive and unweighted. Average BMI does
not measure the percentage of people with obesity.

**Source:** A6 `table1.csv`; prepared NHANES classroom
snapshot [@cdc-nhanes].

## Limitation And Next Step

**Limitation:** This comparison cannot show that income causes BMI differences. It does not account for how NHANES sampled participants, and excluding missing information may affect the results.

**Next step:** Before using this pattern to guide a decision, check whether it remains after accounting for how NHANES selected participants, examining which records were left out because BMI or income was missing, and considering age differences between income groups.

**AI-use note:** AI was not used for this part
